Also, $3$ girl children are born in September for every $2$ boy children where as the ratio is the same for every other month. Given then Kavya (assume female gender) is born in Rebuke what is the probability that her birthday is in September? (up to $3$ decimal places)

The propagation delay between $X$ and $Y$ is $60$ milliseconds. What should be the minimum window size $X$ should use to maximize the line utilization? Assume that the acknowledgement frame is of negligible size and processing delay may be ignored.

Anjana, Chandani, and Pooja are three students that took the Logic exam. Let’s consider a propositional language where $p$ represents “Anjana passed the exam”, $q$ represents “Chandani passed the exam” and $r$ represents "Pooja passed the exam".

  2. $p \wedge q \wedge r$
  3. $(p \wedge q \wedge \neg r )\vee (\neg p \wedge q \wedge r)\vee (p \wedge \neg q \wedge r)$

The time complexity of the following C snippet is:

int gate_2020(int n)
{
    for(int i=1; i <= n; i++)
    {
        for(int j=i ; j<=i*i ; j++)
            if(j%i==0)
            {
                for(int k=0; k < j; k++)
                    printf("gate2020");
            }
    }
}
  1. $\Theta(n^3)$
  2. $\Theta (n^2)$
  3. $\Theta(n^4)$
  4. $\Theta(n^5)$

Consider the C code fragment given below:

....

Assume that $a$ matrix is not in cache at the beginning of the loop given variable $d$ is in a register and starting addresses of $a$ is at cache line boundary. Suppose the compiler does an loop interchange optimization to interchange the $i$ and $j$ loops without any other code change in the loop as follows.

#define N 1000

....

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}\hline \textbf{A} & \textbf{B} & \textbf{C}
\\\hline \text{2} & \text{3} & \text{4}
\\\hline \text{4} & \text{6} & \text{5}
\\\hline \text{5} & \text{4} & \text{6}
\\\hline \text{4} & \text{6} & \text{2}
\\\hline \text{3} & \text{2} & \text{5}

Consider the following SQL query over the Staff, Branch relations given below with Primary Keys being underlined:

  • $\text{Staff:} \underline{\text{ID}}, \text{Name}, \text{position}, \text{branchNo}$
  • $\text{Branch:} \underline{\text{branchNo}}, \text{Name},\text{city}$
SELECT s.Name,b.Name
FROM Staff s, Branch b
WHERE s.branchNo = b.branchNo AND
(s.position = 'Manager' AND b.city = 'New Delhi');

Which of the following queries give the same result as the above SQL query? (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. $\pi_{\text{Staff.Name},\text{Branch.Name}}(\sigma_{ ( \text{position = 'Manager'}) \wedge ( \text{city ='New Delhi'}) \wedge ( \text{Staff.branchNo} = \text{Branch.branchNo} )}$
    $( \text{Staff} \times \text{Branch} ))$
  2. $\pi_{\text{Staff.Name},\text{Branch.Name}}(\sigma_{ ( \text{position ='Manager'}) \wedge ( \text{city ='New Delhi'})}$
    $( \text{Staff} \bowtie_{\text{Staff.branchNo} = \text{Branch.branchNo}} \text{Branch}) )$
  3. SELECT s.Name,b.Name
FROM Staff s JOIN Branch b
on s.branchNo = b.branchNo
WHERE
(s.position = 'Manager' AND b.city = 'New Delhi');

  4. SELECT s.Name,b.Name
FROM Staff s JOIN Branch b
on s.branchNo = b.branchNo
AND
(s.position = 'Manager' AND b.city = 'New Delhi');

Consider the following C program:

#include<stdio.h>
int (*foo(int (*f)(int,int))) (int, int)
{
    return f+1;
}
int fun1(int x,int y)
{
    return x+y;
}
int fun2(int x,int y)
{
    return x*y;
}
int main()
{
    int (*fun_ptr[2])(int,int);
    int x,y;
    fun_ptr[0]=fun1;
    x=fun_ptr[0](4,5);
    fun_ptr[1]=fun2;
    fun_ptr[0] = foo(fun_ptr[0]);
    y=fun_ptr[0](4,5);
    printf("%d %d",x,y);
    return 0;
}

What will be the output when the above program is executed?

  1. $4\;\; 5$
  2. $20\;\; 9$
  3. $9\;\; 20$
  4. None of these

};
